we have demonstrated the feasibility of a new class of digital PLL architectures based on a multibit DTC and a one-bit TCD, which can achieve spur performances close to those of the state-of-the-art analog PLLs.

a digital PLL with a DTC-based one-bit TDC can achieve a spur performance comparable to a conventional PLL with a multibit TDC, while dissipating 2-3 orders of magnitude less power and having a much lower phase noise.
a digital PLL based on a one bit TDC driven by an adaptive DTC can be used for the implementation of low-power frequency synthesizers with low spur levels.

the design of a new digital PLL architecture that combines a one-bit TCD with a multibit DTC, and the development of an adaptive background pre-distortion technique that mitigates the DTC nonlinearity.
the design of a digital fractional-N PLL based on a DTC.
the mitigation of the DTC nonlinearity in digital PLLs, which is one of the main sources of spurs.

this work presents a new digital PLL architecture, based on a one bit TDC and a multi bit DTC.

the proposed DTC pre-distortion scheme is a viable and effective technique to improve the spur performance of the DTC architecture, without compromising the PLL phase noise or power consumption, and is particularly suitable for the design of digital fractional-N synthesizers for high-performance applications.
the proposed pre-distortion technique can be applied to a wide class of digital PLL architectures, and it is a powerful tool to reduce the DTC nonlinearity effects.

the use of a DTC in a digital PLL is not only compatible with low power consumption and good phase noise, but can also lead to spur performance that is competitive with the best analog PLLs.

, for the first time, digital PLLs are able to match the spur performance of their analog counterparts, thus making the digital approach an attractive alternative in the design of low-phase-noise, low-power frequency synthesizers.
